title: "Study 06E — SBayesRC implementation concordance"

## Question and registered amendment

Study 11 asks whether `sblr` reproduces the annotation, SNP, and alpha
behavior of the original official `zhilizheng/SBayesRC` v0.2.6 implementation
on the exact frozen Study 10 data. Production GCTB 2.5.5 remains optional
Phase B. This is a posterior-geometry and implementation-concordance study,
not a method ranking.

The four registered arms are O (official `a=4,b=4`, flat intercept), M
(`sblr` matched flat intercept), P (`sblr` `a=4,b=4`, proper intercept), and
S10 (`sblr` `a=2,b=2`, proper intercept). The induced-stability addendum was
registered after P/S10 checkpoints existed but before their scientific
outputs were inspected or summary tables were emitted.

## Contracts

All frozen Study 10 identities passed. The source-audited official update is
`(sum(alpha_nonintercept^2)+4)/chisq(p+4)`; current `sblr` implements
`(sum(alpha_nonintercept^2)+b)/chisq(p+a)`, proving the `a=4,b=4` mapping.
Annotation order, continuation-stick orientation, eligible sets, latent signs,
and unstandardized annotation values match.

Both routes use the same 35 block correlation matrices. Both retained 984 of
1,000 modes in every block under the 0.995 positive-eigenvalue-mass rule, and
the retained rule-level LD reconstructions had zero normalized Frobenius
difference. Byte-identical independently exposed eigenvectors are not claimed.

## Arm M separation result

O completed its registered 9,000/3,000 single native trajectory. M stopped at
the supported legacy-flat safety guard when an annotation regression became
completely separated (complete separation). The guard was preserved.

The exact exception-local iteration, stick, eligible count, continuation
count, alpha state, `sigmaSqAlpha`, expected probabilities/counts, and realized
occupancy cannot be recovered: current `sblr` serializes failure state only for
residual-scale exceptions, not this annotation exception. A deterministic
same-seed one-iteration replay passed, bounding the event to iterations
2–9,000. After iteration 1 its sigma values were 0.415/0.930/0.507, expected
component counts were 33,982.7/503.8/293.6/219.8, and realized occupancies were
33,939/547/330/184. Further replay would not expose the missing exception-local
state without a package diagnostic capability and was not used to bypass the
guard.

## P versus S10: alpha-prior sensitivity

P and S10 completed four independent chains at the registered 9,000 total,
3,000 burn-in schedule. P did not improve alpha convergence:

| endpoint | P: `a=4,b=4` | S10: `a=2,b=2` |
|---|---:|---:|
| worst nonintercept alpha R-hat | 1.937 | 1.566 |
| median nonintercept bulk ESS | 11.8 | 20.5 |
| minimum nonintercept bulk ESS | 5.70 | 7.26 |
| expected-active R-hat | 1.561 | 1.447 |
| expected active count | 2,154 | 804 |
| minimum chain active-prior Pearson | 0.702 | 0.915 |
| minimum chain active-prior Spearman | -0.072 | 0.910 |

The `a=4,b=4` hierarchy therefore does **not** resolve joint alpha/allocation
mixing under the proper intercept. It was worse on the registered worst-R-hat
and median-ESS summaries, so the Study 10 `a=2,b=2` prior is not supported as
the explanation for the mixing problem. This does not isolate an intercept
effect because both P and S10 intentionally share the same proper intercept.

## Raw alpha versus induced quantities

All low-dimensional induced quantities were reconstructed per retained draw
and chain: component and active expected counts, enriched-versus-unenriched and
continuous top-versus-bottom-quartile probability contrasts, AnnoCondProb and
AnnoJointProb equivalents, and realized allocation counts. Marker-level
component and active priors were summarized by correlations, rank
correlations, RMSE, top-k overlap, and aggregate agreement between chain means.

For both P and S10, poor raw-alpha convergence materially propagated into the
induced prior. P expected-active chain means ranged from 1,445 to 2,559 and its
enriched active-prior contrast from 0.188 to 0.423. S10 expected-active chain
means ranged from 487 to 967 and its enriched contrast from 0.073 to 0.160.
Expected-active and contrast R-hats remained 1.35–1.64. This is not the pattern
of a stable effective prior hidden beneath ridge-like raw alpha; induced
annotation inference itself remains chain-sensitive, particularly for P.

Instability was progressively attenuated downstream. P/S10 posterior mean beta
Pearson was 0.9996 (RMSE 0.00011), with 100% top-100 effect overlap. Their
validation genetic-value correlations were 0.8101 and 0.8095 and phenotype
prediction correlations 0.5703 and 0.5696. PIP Pearson was lower at 0.883
(RMSE 0.075), although top-100 PIP overlap was 0.97. Per-iteration marker beta,
PIP, and prediction histories are not retained by the current block-eigen
result, so these downstream comparisons use posterior endpoints and are not
presented as draw-wise convergence diagnostics.

## Official descriptive comparison

Official alpha lag-1 autocorrelation ranged from 0.975 to 0.9999 and
single-trajectory ESS from about 1.35 to 39.5; several coefficients drifted by
more than one posterior SD between the first and final thirds. This is
descriptive within-trajectory instability, not multichain convergence.

O/P posterior mean beta was highly concordant (Pearson 0.9974; top-100 overlap
0.97), but PIP concordance was only 0.767 and expected active counts were 606
versus 2,152. AnnoCondProb-equivalent quantities also differed. Because O is
flat-intercept and P is proper-intercept, these differences are explicitly
descriptive and cannot be attributed solely to implementation.

## Decision

**A4B4-DOES-NOT-RESOLVE-MIXING.** Changing from the Study 10 `a=2,b=2`
alpha-variance hierarchy to the original `a=4,b=4` hierarchy does not resolve
joint alpha/allocation mixing under the proper intercept. Both raw alpha and
induced annotation-prior quantities remain unstable; beta and prediction are
much more stable downstream, while PIP retains a visible prior sensitivity.

The official trajectory shows similarly difficult alpha exploration, which is
consistent with shared posterior geometry, but exact O-versus-M implementation
concordance remains contract-blocked by M's flat-intercept separation result.
No `sblr` change is made or implied by this benchmark, and no reference capsule
is promoted.
